The strongest provisional direction remains **candidate-softmax training within the supplied corrected BERT4Rec**. Neither User Diagnosis nor Model Diagnosis was supplied; no proposal satisfies diagnosis-qualified selection. This recommendation is an experimental hypothesis.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, terminal-prefix supervision matches appended-mask serving. Its target and later interactions must remain absent from bidirectional input. Second, protected dropout perturbs older context while retaining recent observations. Matched deletion counts are necessary for attributing benefits to recency protection. Third, separately normalized terminal/interior losses make branch weights interpretable. Changing reductions alongside objectives would confound comparisons.

**Insights from related work.** First, [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) motivates objective research but does not establish softmax superiority here. Its positive weighting changes gradient balance. Second, [Correcting the LogQ Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) separates deterministic positives from sampled negatives. History exclusions still prevent full-catalog coverage. Third, [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) motivates historical temporal context. Supervised-target timestamps must remain hidden.

**Framework and candidate assessment.** Directions address candidate competition, temporal relevance, and contextual robustness. Scores are Originality / Potential / User alignment / Model alignment / Difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Alignment remains unavailable.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform candidate softmax | 3/6/NA/NA/4 | Small change coupling candidate rankings | Established objective; optimization scales differ |
| Historical time-gap attention bias | 5/7/NA/NA/7 | Uses observed spacing within one network | Timestamp masking and serving require architectural work |
| Protected-recent dropout | 3/5/NA/NA/3 | Minimal regularization with attributable controls | Recency policy and positional effects can interact |

These scores describe promise, not demonstrated utility. The matched-count dropout experiment remains valuable; holes and compaction require separate comparisons because compaction changes positional embeddings.

**Provisional experiment.** At 40% progress, compare inherited loss and candidate softmax with identical K=16 uniform replacement draws, exclusions, augmentation, reductions, and schedules. Compute `cross_entropy([positive_logit, negative_logits], target=0)` per supervised target, retaining example and branch averaging. Preserve duplicates: multiplicity changes denominator weight. This is sampled candidate classification, without full-catalog calibration guarantees [Blanc and Rendle, 2018](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a.html).

At zero logits, candidate-averaged BCE gives positive gradient −1/34 and each negative +1/34; softmax gives −16/17 and +1/17. No scalar reconciles both. Establish the inherited loss first; prespecify budgeted scale/reweighting controls and matched learning-rate opportunities before claiming objective superiority. Log gradients, clipping, update norms, compute, and every attempted outcome.

Preserve raw serving scores, reserved MASK, left padding, and final-nonpadding readout. Train independently from scratch with one selected checkpoint per category and all four routes. Retain seeds, 200 batches/epoch, the 200-epoch ceiling, predictor writer, diagnostic interfaces, and host macro validation HR@10 selection. Popularity shortcuts and repeated validation selection remain risks. Current diagnoses are required before asserting coverage of two user failures and one measured model failure.

idea.description: Provisionally test K=16 uniform candidate-softmax training in corrected BERT4Rec, retaining one independently trained model and one selected checkpoint per category. Strengthen attribution with prespecified optimization controls when the shared budget permits. This is not a diagnosis-qualified best idea because both supplied diagnoses are absent.
idea.motivation: Candidate softmax couples the positive score directly to sampled alternatives without changing the BERT4Rec backbone or inference scores. Unlike candidate-averaged BCE, its positive and aggregate negative logit gradients balance, and higher-scoring negatives receive greater weight. This motivates a controlled experiment, not an established accuracy improvement. The supplied historical gBCE score supports exploring objectives but cannot establish causality or be reused as a matched control. Neither current user-facing failures nor measured model-facing failures are available, so their alignment remains unassessable. Retain the matched-count protected-dropout direction as a useful alternative; historical time-gap attention is more ambitious and entails greater integration risk.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the supplied corrected baseline. Its executable source is absent from the prompt, so this is an integration specification rather than a replacement standalone train.py. Do not inspect files, execute training, or invent baseline details during this response. Before execution, resolve the supplied baseline's actual loss, negative count, exclusions, positional convention, reductions, optimizer, validation cadence, checkpoint rule and protected-dropout configuration from the host-provided implementation. Record those settings explicitly. An inherited loss must not automatically be labeled candidate-averaged BCE or gBCE.

Prespecify a primary comparison between the inherited objective and candidate softmax using K=16 identical negative draws. If establishing this comparison changes inherited sampling or normalization, disclose the common change; it is then a matched-control experiment rather than an unchanged-baseline comparison. An unchanged baseline reference is a separate budgeted experiment. Preserve initialization, users, endpoints, interior masks, augmentation decisions, batch identities, model dropout policy and update counts using dedicated deterministic RNG streams. No trained checkpoint from another trial may be inspected or reused.

Use the baseline's training-only exclusion policy, explicitly excluding PAD, MASK and the current target. If that policy excludes known history positives, preserve it and document exactly which training events define the exclusion set. Do not use held-out interactions. For every supervised target define A(x,y), require it to be nonempty, and draw K=16 negatives independently and uniformly WITH replacement. Retain every duplicate contribution; do not deduplicate. Record eligible-set sizes, exclusions and duplicate counts. Do not introduce mixed in-batch sampling, temperature tuning, LogQ corrections or additional fitted scores in this first experiment.

For raw candidate softmax, compute logsumexp([s_positive, s_negative_1, ..., s_negative_K]) - s_positive in float32. This optimizes expected sampled-candidate classification, generally different from full-catalog likelihood. A negative appearing m times contributes m*exp(s), equivalent to adding log(m) to its grouped denominator logit. Deduplication therefore changes the objective. Target-dependent history exclusions also change candidate support and can make training negatives easier than host candidates. Do not claim that increasing K or adding a constant LogQ adjustment restores full-catalog consistency.

If importance correction is investigated later, keep the deterministically included positive unchanged and use each sampled negative's actual conditional proposal probability. Subtracting log(K*q(j|x,y)) from negative logits yields an unbiased partition estimate only for the supported universe {y} union A. The logged loss and normalized gradient remain generally biased at finite K. Omitted history items have zero support and cannot be recovered by importance weighting. The refined LogQ paper does not establish finite-K unbiasedness or resolve arbitrary history exclusions. Such a corrected objective is a distinct, separately budgeted experiment.

The main optimization confound must be explicit. Candidate-averaged BCE is [softplus(-s_positive) + sum softplus(s_negative)]/(K+1). At zero logits with K=16, its positive gradient is -1/34 and each negative gradient is +1/34. Candidate softmax gives -16/17 and +1/17 respectively: 32 times the positive magnitude and twice each negative magnitude. These are logit derivatives, not parameter-update ratios. No global scalar matches both. Published gBCE multiplies the BCE positive term by beta=1-t+t*K/(|I|-1) under its catalog assumptions; an eligible-set substitute is a weighting heuristic requiring separate justification.

Keep the initial raw-objective comparison at the same inherited optimizer settings, but describe its conclusion as performance under those settings. Before inspecting results, allocate any available secondary budget to optimization controls. If the reference is candidate-averaged BCE, 2*BCE tests matching softmax's initial per-negative derivative, while positive weight 16 tests its initial positive-to-aggregate-negative balance; applying both matches all initial logit derivatives. These matches hold at zero logits, not throughout training. If the inherited objective differs, derive appropriate controls from its actual expression rather than importing these constants. Give compared objectives equal prespecified learning-rate opportunities, using the same fixed multiplicative grid around the inherited rate if affordable. Do not begin a large factorial search without a measured compute estimate. If controls or learning-rate comparisons cannot fit the remaining 43,200 GPU-second budget, retain the primary comparison and explicitly limit mechanistic claims.

Log loss components, positive and aggregate-negative logit-gradient magnitudes, parameter-gradient norms before clipping, clipping frequency and actual parameter-update norms on a fixed diagnostic subset at a prespecified cadence. Actual update norms are measured from parameter changes, not inferred from learning rate. Adam normalization, optimizer epsilon, clipping and weight decay complicate equivalence between loss scaling and learning-rate scaling. Keep K=16 initially. If K changes later, state whether gBCE beta or t is fixed and account for the resulting changes in competition, weighting and compute.

Retain masked-target terminal/interior sampling, the inherited protected-dropout configuration, separately normalized branch reductions, objective-weight schedule, optimizer, validation cadence and checkpoint policy. Average valid supervised targets within each example and then examples within each branch, provided that is the supplied corrected reduction; otherwise establish and disclose the common repair first. Terminal targets and all later events must be absent before the reserved MASK is appended. Every supervised interior target must be hidden. No target timestamp or target text enters a masked position. Earlier observed repetitions of the same item remain legitimate history.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch, at most 200 epochs, single-GPU execution, Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Honor the environment's 200-epoch default. Use the same prespecified horizon, validation cadence, checkpoint opportunities and inherited deterministic tie-breaking rule across compared arms. All controls, incomplete runs, diagnostics and failures consume the shared budget. Each executed arm initializes one model per category from scratch and exports exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Never combine arms, average checkpoints or add independently fitted scorers.

Inference continues to use raw model logits from intact observed histories plus an appended reserved MASK. Truncate observed history to reserve room for MASK, then left-pad. Read the greatest nonpadding index, never nonpadding-count minus one. For fixed-width examples with terminal MASK, this is the last slot. Preserve PAD-key exclusion at every attention layer. Save architecture configuration, item mapping, PAD/MASK IDs, maxlen and the selected state_dict. Preserve the canonical predictor writer with strict checkpoint loading and verify trained, reloaded, ModelView and exported predictor score parity on short, singleton, full-length, truncated and mixed-length histories, including existing ranking checks. Training-only augmentation is disabled at serving.

Keep view.model as the actual trained module and retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Set dataset identity to the actual routed category. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The public diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B x L tensors; internal multi-negative training must not alter that interface. Use a separate-RNG frozen, unaugmented training panel. Record terminal/interior sampled margins and negative-beats-positive rates with counts and definitions. Gate serving-dependent probes on parity. These proposed measurements are not supplied findings and cannot establish full-catalog calibration.

Monitor training-derived frequency and history-length strata for popularity shortcuts and sparse-item degradation without fitting an additional scorer. Known-positive exclusions do not identify all false negatives, and high-scoring unobserved items are not verified positives. Preserve the twenty-real-user full-catalog simulator protocol without inventing preferences, compatibility, ownership, diversity or conformity traits. Only public interaction histories, titles, descriptions and historical timestamps are available; this experiment uses histories alone. No unavailable reviews, ratings, categories, prices or stores, pretrained weights, extra datasets or hidden test information may be introduced.

For the alternative protected-dropout direction, distinguish deletion policy from representation. Compare recency-protected versus uniform deletion with identical per-example removal counts within fixed-position PAD holes; keep terminal MASK fixed and exclude PAD keys. A separately budgeted holes/compaction factorial plus an unaugmented reference can reveal positional interactions. Compaction preserves order but generally changes surviving slot positions; a compacted view carrying original position IDs is an optional further control. PAD holes are not attended MASK tokens. Do not claim that improvement over no augmentation alone isolates recency preservation. IeSRec and SETO are related precedents, not evidence for the exact matched-count comparison.

Only the host's pinned macro validation HR@10 selects configurations. Retain 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42 through the unchanged evaluator; training duplicates do not alter evaluation candidates. Prespecify comparisons and report all attempted outcomes, GPU seconds, completed updates and selection opportunities. Repeated trial/checkpoint selection can overfit the fixed validation panel. Do not report a sampled-metric gain as full-catalog superiority. Current diagnoses are still required before any idea can satisfy the mandatory two-user-failure and one-model-failure qualification.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def candidate_softmax_loss(positive_logits, negative_logits):
    """Return per-target sampled-candidate cross-entropy.

    positive_logits: (...,)
    negative_logits: (..., K)
    Uniform replacement draws retain duplicate contributions.
    This is not an unbiased full-catalog likelihood estimator.
    """
    if negative_logits.ndim != positive_logits.ndim + 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected negative logits shaped (..., K)')
    if negative_logits.shape[:-1] != positive_logits.shape:
        raise ValueError('Positive and negative target dimensions differ')
    if negative_logits.shape[-1] < 1:
        raise ValueError('At least one negative is required')
    logits = torch.cat([
        positive_logits.float().unsqueeze(-1),
        negative_logits.float(),
    ], dim=-1)
    targets = torch.zeros(logits.shape[:-1], device=logits.device,
                          dtype=torch.long)
    return F.cross_entropy(
        logits.reshape(-1, logits.shape[-1]),
        targets.reshape(-1), reduction='none'
    ).reshape(positive_logits.shape)


def candidate_averaged_bce(positive_logits, negative_logits,
                           positive_weight=1.0, scale=1.0):
    """Optional explicit control; do not assume this is inherited loss."""
    if negative_logits.ndim != positive_logits.ndim + 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected negative logits shaped (..., K)')
    if negative_logits.shape[:-1] != positive_logits.shape:
        raise ValueError('Positive and negative target dimensions differ')
    k = negative_logits.shape[-1]
    if k < 1:
        raise ValueError('At least one negative is required')
    return float(scale) * (
        float(positive_weight) * F.softplus(-positive_logits.float())
        + F.softplus(negative_logits.float()).sum(dim=-1)
    ) / (k + 1)


# Integration specification: use the supplied corrected baseline source.
# Resolve and record inherited configuration before executing experiments.
# Prespecify primary arms: inherited objective and candidate softmax.
# Pair K=16 uniform-with-replacement negative draws across arms.
# Disclose any common sampling/reduction change from the original baseline.
#
# Optional controls, only if reference is candidate-averaged BCE:
#   raw BCE:                positive_weight=1,  scale=1
#   scalar-rescaled BCE:    positive_weight=1,  scale=2
#   positive-reweighted:    positive_weight=16, scale=1
#   combined initial match: positive_weight=16, scale=2
# The combined control matches softmax logit derivatives only at zero logits.
# Budget and choose controls before seeing outcomes; never fuse their scores.
# Prespecify equal learning-rate opportunities if remaining compute permits.
# Otherwise limit conclusions to the inherited optimizer configuration.
#
# Use dedicated seed-42 RNG streams for initialization, users/endpoints,
# masks, augmentation, negatives and diagnostic sampling. Keep model dropout
# consumption paired independently of loss-specific computations.
#
# For each independently executed arm and each of the four categories:
#   initialize ONE corrected BERT4Rec from scratch with training seed 42
#   for epoch in range(prespecified_horizon <= 200):
#       for step in range(200):
#           terminal, interior = supplied_leakage_free_sampler()
#           preserve inherited protected dropout and positional convention
#           for each supervised target:
#               A = actual baseline training-only eligible negative set
#               exclude PAD, MASK and target; require len(A) > 0
#               negatives = uniform_draw(A, 16, replacement=True)
#               retain duplicates and record eligibility/duplicate counts
#               compute selected per-target objective in float32
#           Lt = inherited_example_and_branch_reduction(terminal_losses)
#           Li = inherited_example_and_branch_reduction(interior_losses)
#           loss = inherited_alpha(epoch)*Lt + (1-inherited_alpha(epoch))*Li
#           optimize with unchanged clipping/scheduler/regularization rules
#           at prespecified diagnostic cadence:
#               record logit-gradient contributions and parameter grad norms
#               record clipping and actual parameter-change norms
#       apply unchanged validation cadence and checkpoint selection
#   save ONE selected checkpoint with exact architecture/configuration
#   export through canonical predictor writer with strict loading
#   verify trained/reloaded/ModelView/exported score and ranking parity
#   run compatible frozen diagnostics with measured values and definitions
#   record GPU seconds, completed updates and checkpoint opportunities
#
# Serving: observed history[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK], then left padding.
# Read greatest nonpadding position; score candidates with raw model logits.
# Preserve ModelView and DiagnosisProbe public contracts, including the
# B x L diagnostic loader even though training uses K negatives internally.
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed remains 0.
# Preserve all four category routes, host splits/evaluator and trial paths.
# All controls/failures count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.
# No score fusion, checkpoint averaging, independent auxiliary scorers,
# other-trial checkpoint reuse, or hidden test access.

originality.positive: A matched-sampling and optimization-aware comparison provides a focused experiment within corrected terminal/interior BERT4Rec.
originality.negative: Candidate softmax, gradient reweighting and sampled classification are established; careful controls improve attribution rather than creating a new objective.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could guide sampling and objective design without increasing inference complexity, and clarify whether improvements arise from candidate competition or weighting.
future_potential.negative: Accuracy gains, diagnosis alignment and full-catalog transfer remain unverified; small validation panels and optimization interactions limit generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: The core loss and optional BCE controls are short stable expressions requiring no architecture or serving change.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful baseline integration, paired random streams, update diagnostics, budgeted controls and serialization parity require more work than the loss expression alone suggests.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes masked-item training with a bidirectional Transformer and appended-mask sequential inference.
Uses learned positional embeddings, motivating explicit treatment of deletion-induced reindexing.
limitations: Does not establish candidate softmax superiority on the pinned four-category benchmark.
Does not isolate the proposed matched-count recency-deletion comparison.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates studying sampled BCE overconfidence and positive-term weighting in sequential recommendation.
Provides a reference for distinguishing weighting changes from global loss scaling.
limitations: Does not directly validate candidate softmax in corrected BERT4Rec.
Calibration reasoning requires sampling assumptions that arbitrary history exclusions may violate.

related_work.title: gSASRec authors' implementation
contributions: Supplies loss definitions for checking BCE and gBCE weighting and deriving logit gradients.
limitations: Implementation details and reductions must be checked against the actual supplied baseline.
Logit-gradient ratios do not establish parameter-update ratios or ranking gains.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes deterministically included positives from sampled negatives.
Develops negative-only importance normalization and an uncertainty-related stop-gradient weighting.
limitations: Does not recover omitted catalog support under arbitrary history exclusions.
Does not establish finite-K unbiased loss or gradients for the proposed conditional sampler.

related_work.title: Adaptive Sampled Softmax with Kernel Based Sampling
contributions: Studies sampled-softmax estimation and proposal-dependent bias.
Provides context for distinguishing sampled candidate classification from full-catalog likelihood.
limitations: Does not validate this benchmark-specific uncorrected candidate objective.
An unbiased supported partition estimate does not imply an unbiased logged loss or normalized gradient.

related_work.title: SASRec and BERT4Rec sampled-objective implementation
contributions: Provides implementation context for sampled objectives in sequential recommendation.
limitations: A reproducible comparison must record the exact loss reduction and code version used.
Repository precedent alone does not establish gains under the pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces historical time intervals into sequential attention.
limitations: Transfer to bidirectional BERT4Rec requires target-timestamp masking and compatible serving and diagnostic interfaces.
Does not establish gains for the proposed temporal alternative on these four datasets.

related_work.title: IeSRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes earliest-interaction deletion to preserve recent behavior and reports BERT4Rec improvements.
limitations: The supplied evidence does not establish recency-preserving versus uniform deletion with identical per-example removal counts.
Its reported gains cannot isolate positional representation effects in the proposed experiment.

related_work.title: SETO
contributions: The supplied search summary describes random interaction removal with compaction and left padding.
limitations: Compaction changes positional assignments and therefore differs from fixed-position PAD holes.
Does not establish the exact matched-count recency-protection hypothesis.
